title: Chicken breast, baked or broiled, skin eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken breast is a lean cut of poultry meat, rich in protein and low in fat. In this product the breast is pre‑cooked (baked or broiled) and served with the skin, which keeps it juicy and adds flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken breast is the most popular protein source in many countries.
Baking or broiling with the skin helps retain more B‑vitamins.
The skin provides beneficial monounsaturated fats and collagen.
Pre‑cooked breast is convenient for storage and quick reheating.
In the United States chicken breast is a staple of many diet plans because of its low calorie density.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 31 g of complete protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: When cooked without added oil, the breast remains low‑fat, supporting cardiovascular health.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B3 (niacin) and B6 aid energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals: phosphorus and selenium
items.content: Phosphorus contributes to bone health, while selenium offers antioxidant protection.

items.title: Collagen from the skin
items.content: The skin contains collagen, which supports skin, hair and joint health.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improper storage or insufficient reheating can allow bacteria such as Salmonella to grow.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium content in processed versions
items.content: Some pre‑cooked products contain added salt; individuals with hypertension should check labels.

items.title: Fat in the skin
items.content: While flavorful, the skin adds extra calories and saturated fat.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reheat the chicken breast in the microwave, on a skillet, or in the oven. Slice it for salads, sandwiches, add to pasta, or use in quick‑prep meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked breast in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in a freezer‑safe bag for 2‑3 months. Heat thoroughly to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.
